title: Compact-object and Ind duality for a fixed accessibility rank
statement: Let $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal. Let $\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty$ be the subcategory of the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of $\mathcal U'$-small infinity categories (the homotopy coherent nerve of quasicategories with the cores of their functor simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], formed in a further universe) whose objects are the presentable infinity categories that are $\lambda$-accessible and whose morphisms are the coherent functors preserving small colimits and $\lambda$-compact objects, and let $\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm R,\lambda}_\infty$ be the subcategory with the same objects whose morphisms are the coherent functors admitting a left adjoint and preserving small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. (1) For objects $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and an adjunction $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:R$, the functor $L$ preserves $\lambda$-compact objects if and only if $R$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; every functor between objects preserving small colimits has a right adjoint. (2) There is an equivalence $\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty\simeq(\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm R,\lambda}_\infty)^{\mathrm{op}}$ which is the identity on objects and carries each morphism $L$ to a right adjoint of $L$; hence for every small infinity category $S$, coherent diagrams $S\to\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty$ correspond, up to equivalence, to coherent diagrams $S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm R,\lambda}_\infty$ with the same values, each arrow being sent to a right adjoint of it. (3) Let $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ be the infinity category of small infinity categories admitting $\lambda$-small colimits, with functors preserving these colimits. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda$ of [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], sending $C$ to $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ and $u:C\to D$ to the extension of $C\xrightarrow{u}D\xrightarrow{j}\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ preserving small $\lambda$-filtered colimits, is an equivalence of infinity categories $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty\to\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty$. A quasi-inverse sends $\mathcal C$ to a small infinity category equivalent to the full subcategory $\mathcal C^\lambda$ of $\lambda$-compact objects of $\mathcal C$ and a morphism to its restriction to $\lambda$-compact objects, and the Yoneda embedding identifies $C$ with $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)^\lambda$. Being equivalences of infinity categories, these equivalences act on coherent diagrams including all higher simplices. The universes, compactness, accessibility and presentability used here are those of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and adjunctions, coherent functors and subcategories are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

proof.text: First construct the compact model of a presentable $\lambda$-accessible category $\mathcal C$. Choose an essentially small full generating subcategory $G$ of $\lambda$-compact objects as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Every $\lambda$-compact $c$ is a homotopy retract of an object of $G$: present $c$ as a small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of $G$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-compact-stage-factorization] to $1_c$. The retract-size clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus] makes the full subcategory $\mathcal C^\lambda$ essentially small. Since $\mathcal C$ is cocomplete, [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] says it is closed under $\lambda$-small colimits computed in $\mathcal C$. Take a small model $A\simeq\mathcal C^\lambda$ and write $i:A\to\mathcal C$ for its fully faithful inclusion through this equivalence. It preserves $\lambda$-small colimits, and every object of $\mathcal C$ is a small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of objects of $i(A)$, because $G$ is contained in that image.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.4.2.2, Lemma 5.4.2.4, Remark 5.4.2.11 and the opening paragraph of 5.5.7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] with $\kappa=\lambda$ and the fully faithful $i:A\to\mathcal C$ of step 1. Its values are $\lambda$-compact and generate by small $\lambda$-filtered colimits, so its extension $e:\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(A)\to\mathcal C$ is an equivalence. The target is presentable and $i$ preserves $\lambda$-small colimits, so the last clause of the same node makes $e$ colimit-preserving. In particular compact objects detect equivalences in $\mathcal C$: if $v:x\to y$ induces equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(i(a),x)\to\operatorname{Map}(i(a),y)$ for every $a$, then present any object $t$ as a filtered colimit of $i(a)$; the mapping-space colimit criterion identifies $\operatorname{Map}(t,v)$ with a limit of these equivalences. Yoneda then detects that $v$ is an equivalence. This argument uses small presentations one at a time, never a limit over the large category $\mathcal C$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.3.5.11 and Definition 5.5.7.1, with the compact-generator detection calculation.

proof.text:
For clause (1), let $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:R$ be the given adjunction. If $R$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits, then for a compact $c$ the functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lc,-)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,R-)$ preserves them, so $Lc$ is compact. Conversely suppose $L$ preserves compact objects, take a small $\lambda$-filtered diagram $d_i$ in $\mathcal D$, and form the canonical comparison $v:\operatorname{colim}_iRd_i\to R(\operatorname{colim}_id_i)$. For compact $c$, compactness in $\mathcal C$, the adjunction, and compactness of $Lc$ give the chain
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,\operatorname{colim}_iRd_i)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,Rd_i)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lc,d_i)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lc,\operatorname{colim}_id_i)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,R\operatorname{colim}_id_i).$$
These are the maps induced by $v$, so step 2 proves $v$ is an equivalence. Finally [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] supplies the right adjoint to every small-colimit-preserving functor between the presentable categories. A filtered indexing category is nonempty; this calculation does not claim the empty category is filtered.

We next establish the coherent adjoint variance used in clause (2), independently of presentability of a total category. Take a coherent diagram $H:S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ with right-adjoint arrows and unstraighten it to a Cartesian fibration $p:E\to S$, using the opposite of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] in a universe containing the base and all total categories. Write $f^*:E_t\to E_s$ for transport along $f:s\to t$, and choose its left adjoint $f_!$. For $x\in E_s$, the unit $x\to f^*f_!x$ followed by the Cartesian lift $f^*f_!x\to f_!x$ gives $u:x\to f_!x$ over $f$. It is cocartesian: for each $z\in E_v$, compare $\operatorname{Map}_E(f_!x,z)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_S(s,v)}\operatorname{Map}_S(t,v)$. Both lie over $\operatorname{Map}_S(t,v)$. Over $g:t\to v$ the Cartesian mapping criterion (the opposite of the cocartesian criterion) identifies their fibers with $\operatorname{Map}_{E_t}(f_!x,g^*z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{E_s}(x,f^*g^*z)$. The comparison is the adjunction equivalence. Fiber detection over this SAME base proves the comparison is an equivalence, so the mapping criterion proves $u$ is cocartesian. This constructs all cocartesian lifts, making $p$ a bifibration. For the reverse construction, start with a cocartesian fibration with left-adjoint transports $f_!$ and choose right adjoints $f^*$. For $y\in E_t$, compose the cocartesian lift $f^*y\to f_!f^*y$ over $f:s\to t$ with the counit $f_!f^*y\to y$ to obtain $w:f^*y\to y$ over $f$. Test the Cartesian mapping comparison $\operatorname{Map}_E(z,f^*y)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(z,y)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_S(v,t)}\operatorname{Map}_S(v,s)$ for $z\in E_v$. Over $g:v\to s$, cocartesian lifts identify its fibers with $\operatorname{Map}_{E_s}(g_!z,f^*y)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{E_t}(f_!g_!z,y)$; the comparison is the adjunction equivalence. Fiber detection over $\operatorname{Map}_S(v,s)$ and the Cartesian mapping criterion make $w$ Cartesian. This supplies every required Cartesian lift. No accessibility or presentability of $S$ is used.

source.place: HTT Corollaries 5.2.2.4–5.2.2.5; the mapping-space proof of the local-to-global cocartesian criterion.

proof.text: The two straightenings of a bifibration have the same fibers, and on every edge [lem-coef-infinity-bicartesian-interval-adjunction] identifies their transports as an adjoint pair. Thus step 4 and the adjoint existence result give two descriptions of the same equivalence classes of bifibrations over $S$ with presentable fibers: diagrams $S\to\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L}_\infty$ and diagrams $S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm R}_\infty$. Equivalences of total categories over $S$ preserve both Cartesian and cocartesian edges by their mapping-space characterization. Pullback preserves that characterization, and straightening is natural under pullback, so this bijection is natural in $S$. Restrict now to $\lambda$-accessible fibers and the edge condition of step 3, which is the same condition on the two transports. Put $A=\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty$ and $B=(\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm R,\lambda}_\infty)^{\mathrm{op}}$. We have natural bijections $\Phi_S:[S,A]\to[S,B]$, where brackets are equivalence classes of coherent functors. Enlarge the universe to include $A$ and $B$, so they too are permitted test bases. Set $F=\Phi_A([1_A])$ and $G=\Phi_B^{-1}([1_B])$. Naturality for a class $h:S\to A$ gives $\Phi_S(h)=Fh$, and naturality of the inverse gives $\Phi_S^{-1}(k)=Gk$ for $k:S\to B$. Therefore $GF=1_A$ and $FG=1_B$ as classes. Representatives of $F,G$ are coherent functors whose composites are naturally equivalent to the identities, hence an equivalence of infinity categories. Testing on $S=\Delta^0$ and $\Delta^1$ identifies its object values and arrows with the specified fibers and adjoint transports. Finally composing this equivalence and its inverse with diagrams gives inverse equivalences of the full coherent functor categories, since the two natural inverse equivalences can be whiskered with any diagram. This proves clause (2), including higher simplices, without choosing adjoints independently on arrows.

source.place: HTT Definition 5.5.3.2, Proposition 5.5.3.3, Corollary 5.5.3.4 and Notation 5.5.7.7; the natural-bijection/Yoneda inverse calculation and the passage to coherent diagram categories are explicit.

proof.text: For a small $C$ admitting $\lambda$-small colimits, [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability] makes $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ presentable and $\lambda$-accessible, with a fully faithful Yoneda functor $j$ preserving $\lambda$-small colimits and taking values in compact objects. If $x$ is any $\lambda$-compact object of this Ind category, choose its filtered presentation by representables from the same node. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-compact-stage-factorization] to $1_x$: it is a homotopy retract of some $j(c)$. Since $\lambda$ is uncountable, every countable simplicial set is $\lambda$-small. The new general retraction-colimit lemma therefore applies to $j$, proving $x\simeq j(c\prime)$ for some $c\prime\in C$. Hence $j$ identifies $C$ with the full compact subcategory. This is the exact point at which uncountability replaces the separate idempotent-completeness condition; no assertion for $\lambda=\omega$ is made.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.5.7.8, Remark 5.5.7.9 and Proposition 5.5.7.10, expanded via HTT 4.4.5 on retracts.

proof.text: Let $C,D$ be small categories with $\lambda$-small colimits, and let $u:C\to D$ preserve them. The composite $j_Du:C\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ preserves those colimits. Its filtered extension $u_!$ exists, including coherent transformation data, by [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension]. The all-colimits clause of that node makes $u_!$ preserve small colimits. It preserves compact objects because by step 6 every compact source object is represented by some $c$, and $u_!j_C(c)\simeq j_Du(c)$ is compact. Conversely a small-colimit- and compact-object-preserving functor between the two Ind categories restricts under step 6 to such a $u$, preserving $\lambda$-small colimits because the two Yoneda embeddings do. The restriction equivalence of coherent functor categories in [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] restricts to these full subcategories. On cores it gives the equivalence of mapping spaces needed below, including all coherent natural equivalences and their higher homotopies, not a claim that all noninvertible natural transformations become morphisms of $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.3.5.10 and Proposition 5.5.1.9, the mapping-space argument in Proposition 5.5.7.8.

proof.text: Taking the full compact subcategory defines the coherent restriction functor $\theta$ on $\operatorname{Pr}^{\mathrm L,\lambda}_\infty$: restriction acts on functors and on their coherent equivalences and higher homotopies, and respects composition. One can first keep the full essentially small subcategories in the larger universe and then take small models. Step 1 places its values in the essentially small $\lambda$-cocomplete categories; step 2 identifies every source category with the Ind completion of its compact model; step 7 identifies the mapping spaces by restriction. Therefore $\theta$ is fully faithful. Step 6 says every small $\lambda$-cocomplete $C$ is equivalent to $\theta(\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C))$, so $\theta$ is essentially surjective onto these categories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to obtain a coherent quasi-inverse. Under step 7 that quasi-inverse sends $C$ to $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ and $u$ to its filtered extension $u_!$, since the extension space with its restriction identification is contractible. This proves every assertion of clause (3), with small models understood up to equivalence as in the statement. The restriction and extension equivalences, being equivalences of infinity categories, carry the whole coherent diagram for any small $S$; composing with clause (2) gives the asserted right-adjoint diagrams with opposite variance and the same values.
